rubrics.justification: The model appropriately stated that no image was available to it and did not fabricate specific embryo morphology. However, it did not analyze the visible day-4 embryo image, so morphology assessment was omitted rather than matched to the image.

It integrates most relevant factors well: age-related aneuploidy risk, PCOS response, sperm limitations, BMI, endometrium, and lifestyle. Some links are somewhat generic and it assumes a good-quality blastocyst despite the actual day-4 context.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with clear acknowledgment of uncertainty from missing morphology. Minor issues include discussing blastocyst/Gardner grading despite transfer day 4 and basing probability on an assumed good-quality blastocyst.

Most recommendations are broadly evidence-based (single embryo transfer consideration, luteal support, lifestyle optimization, antagonist use in PCOS). However, ERA and adjunctive therapies are weakly supported, and routine strong endorsement of PGT-A at age 37 is more debatable than presented.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including embryo selection, luteal support, counseling, lifestyle changes, and male-factor workup. Some suggestions are somewhat generic and not fully tailored to the day-4 embryo scenario.
